title: Evaluation of an increasing filtered module and its finite presentation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq0$, and $M$ an $A$-module with commuting $A$-linear endomorphisms $T_1,\ldots,T_n$. Let $(F_dM)_{d\geq0}$ be increasing $A$-submodules with $\bigcup_dF_dM=M$ and $T_i(F_dM)\subseteq F_{d+1}M$. Put $P=A[X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ and $Q=A[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Give $N=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}F_dM\,t^d$ the $P$-action $X_0(xt^d)=xt^{d+1}$, $X_i(xt^d)=T_i(x)t^{d+1}$. Give $M$ its $Q$-action $X_i x=T_i(x)$ and its $P$-action via $X_0\mapsto1$, $X_i\mapsto X_i$. Evaluation $\epsilon:N\to M$, $\sum_dx_dt^d\mapsto\sum_dx_d$, is a surjective $P$-linear map with kernel $(X_0-1)N$; its induced isomorphism $N/(X_0-1)N\cong M$ is $Q$-linear via $P/(X_0-1)\cong Q$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. More precisely, for every finite presentation $P^u\xrightarrow{H}P^v\xrightarrow{\pi}N\to0$, the sequence $Q^u\xrightarrow{H(1,X)}Q^v\xrightarrow{\bar\pi}M\to0$ is exact, where $H(1,X)$ is obtained by substituting $X_0=1$ in every matrix entry and $\bar\pi$ sends the $j$th basis vector to $\epsilon(\pi(e_j))$. In particular, if $N$ is finitely presented over $P$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], then $M$ is finitely presented over $Q$.

proof.text: Write $\iota_d(x)=xt^d$ in the finite-support direct sum. Let $S_0\iota_d(x)=\iota_{d+1}(x)$ and $S_i\iota_d(x)=\iota_{d+1}(T_i x)$. These are well-defined $A$-linear maps by the filtration hypotheses. On each summand, $S_0S_i\iota_d(x)=S_iS_0\iota_d(x)=\iota_{d+2}(T_i x)$ and $S_iS_j\iota_d(x)=\iota_{d+2}(T_iT_jx)=S_jS_i\iota_d(x)$. Thus $p=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha X^\alpha$ acts by $p z=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha S_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots S_n^{\alpha_n}z$: distributivity and commutation give $(pq)z=p(qz)$ and $1z=z$. The identical formula with $T_i$ defines the $Q$-action on $M$. Polynomial evaluation defines $\rho:P\to Q$, $X_0\mapsto1$, $X_i\mapsto X_i$; restricting along $\rho$ gives the stated $P$-action on $M$.

proof.text: The finite sum $\epsilon(\sum_d\iota_d(x_d))=\sum_dx_d$ is $A$-linear. For every $z\in N$, $\epsilon(S_0z)=\epsilon(z)$ and $\epsilon(S_iz)=T_i\epsilon(z)$, by summing its components. Applying these identities repeatedly to each monomial and then adding proves $\epsilon(pz)=\rho(p)\epsilon(z)$ for every $p\in P$. Exhaustiveness gives, for each $m\in M$, a $d$ with $m\in F_dM$, so $\epsilon(\iota_d(m))=m$. Hence $\epsilon$ is a surjective $P$-linear map.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, polynomial-module construction and its omitted dehomogenization details; explicit elementary expansion for the increasing filtration used in Tag 053E(2), more-algebra.tex, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation.

proof.text: Since $\epsilon(S_0z-z)=0$, $(X_0-1)N\subseteq\ker\epsilon$. Conversely let $z=\sum_{d=0}^{D}\iota_d(x_d)$ with $\sum_{d=0}^{D}x_d=0$. For $0\leq d<D$ set $y_d=-\sum_{i=0}^{d}x_i\in F_dM$, using the increasing filtration, and put $y=\sum_{d=0}^{D-1}\iota_d(y_d)$. The components of $(S_0-1)y$ are $-y_0=x_0$ in degree $0$, $y_{d-1}-y_d=x_d$ for $0<d<D$, and $y_{D-1}=x_D$ in degree $D$; higher components vanish. If $D=0$, the zero-sum condition gives $z=0$ and take $y=0$. Thus $z=(X_0-1)y$ and $\ker\epsilon=(X_0-1)N$.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, polynomial-module construction and its omitted dehomogenization details; explicit elementary expansion for the increasing filtration used in Tag 053E(2), more-algebra.tex, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation.

proof.text: Let $s:Q\to P$ include the variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$, so $\rho s=1$. Write a polynomial as $p=\sum_{k=0}^{r}s(q_k)X_0^k$. The identity $p-s(\rho(p))=(X_0-1)\sum_{k=1}^{r}s(q_k)(1+X_0+\cdots+X_0^{k-1})$ proves $\ker\rho=(X_0-1)P$. Therefore $[p]\mapsto\rho(p)$ and $q\mapsto[s(q)]$ are mutually inverse ring maps $P/(X_0-1)\cong Q$ of the quotient ring [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. On module cosets define $[z]\mapsto\epsilon(z)$. Step 3 makes this well-defined and injective, and Step 2 makes it surjective. Its inverse sends $m$ to $[z]$ for any lift $\epsilon(z)=m$: any two lifts differ by Step 3, so the coset is independent of the lift. Coset addition and scalar multiplication show that this is a linear isomorphism; in particular $[s(q)z]\mapsto q\epsilon(z)$ proves $Q$-linearity through the displayed ring identification.

proof.text: Fix the given exact presentation, write $h_{ij}$ for the entries of $H$, and define $\bar\pi(a_1,\ldots,a_v)=\sum_j a_j\epsilon(\pi(e_j))$. This is $Q$-linear. For $w\in P^v$, the finite basis expansion and Step 2 give $\bar\pi(\rho^v(w))=\epsilon(\pi(w))$, where $\rho^v$ means entrywise evaluation. For $b\in P^u$, entrywise evaluation respects the matrix sums, so $\rho^v(Hb)=H(1,X)\rho^u(b)$. Consequently $\bar\pi H(1,X)=0$: lift an input by $s^u$ and use $\pi H=0$. Also $\bar\pi$ is surjective: lift $m\in M$ first to $z\in N$ by Step 2, then to $w\in P^v$ by surjectivity of $\pi$; its preimage is $\rho^v(w)$.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, polynomial-module construction and its omitted dehomogenization details; explicit elementary expansion for the increasing filtration used in Tag 053E(2), more-algebra.tex, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation.

proof.text: If $a\in Q^v$ satisfies $\bar\pi(a)=0$, put $w=s^v(a)$. Then $\epsilon(\pi(w))=0$, so Step 3 supplies $y\in N$ with $\pi(w)=(X_0-1)y$. Choose $c\in P^v$ with $\pi(c)=y$. The vector $w-(X_0-1)c$ is in $\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}H$, hence equals $Hb$ for some $b\in P^u$. Evaluating every coordinate yields $a=H(1,X)\rho^u(b)$, since $\rho(X_0-1)=0$. Together with Step 5 this proves exactness at $Q^v$ and $M$, with precisely the specified matrix and augmentation. Finally, if $N$ is finitely presented, choose such finite $u,v$ by the definition. The resulting exact sequence of finite free $Q$-modules is a finite presentation of $M$.
